matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to fix the equation by moving a stick within the same character; many puzzles can be solved by simple intra‑character changes such as turning X into V or V into X before considering inter‑character moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is incorrect, start by checking if moving a stick inside a numeral or operator can produce a valid symbol.
matchstick.example: Attempting to move a stick from one character to another without first trying to change X to V within the same character.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, verify that every resulting character is a recognized Roman numeral or a valid operator; an invalid shape (e.g., a lone diagonal) invalidates the solution.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before checking arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal stick after removing a diagonal from X, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; when moving a diagonal from X or V, ensure the source character still forms a valid numeral (e.g., X→V) rather than leaving a lone diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is removed from a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from V and ending up with an isolated diagonal stick, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign, freeing the vertical stick for reuse elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and a vertical stick could be useful for adjusting a numeral.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' but forgetting to place the freed vertical stick, leaving it unused.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., moving a vertical stick to create an extra I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you have a free stick after modifying an operator or numeral and need to increase the value of a side.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick to the left of V without forming a proper I, resulting in an invalid symbol.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If intra‑character moves fail, explore moving a stick from one character to a different character; many solutions require transferring a stick between numerals or between an operator and a numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Only moving sticks within the same character and never trying to move a stick from one numeral to another.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting '+' to '-', the freed vertical stick can be attached to a nearby numeral (e.g., adding it to V to make IV) to increase its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and the equation needs a larger numeral on one side.
matchstick.example: Converting '+' to '-' but not using the released vertical stick to augment a numeral, missing a valid solution.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides after any transformation; an equation that looks syntactically correct may still be arithmetically false.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming all symbols are valid, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Proposing 'XV - XV = XVI' without checking that 0 ≠ 16.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If you relocate a stick from the '=', ensure the equality sign still consists of two horizontal sticks; otherwise the equation loses a valid '='.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' and leaving the original '=' with only one line, turning it into a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Create trivial equality by duplicating term
matchstick.principle: If you can move a single stick so that the right‑hand side becomes identical to the left‑hand side (or all terms become the same), the equation is trivially true; this often involves turning a subtraction into an equality and adjusting a numeral to match the other side.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When other transformations fail, check whether a single‑stick move can make both sides (or all terms) the same, yielding a chain equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick to obtain 'XV = XV = XV' without ensuring the move respects the single‑stick constraint, leading to an invalid solution.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump straight to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler fixes that stay within a single symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate all possible intra‑character stick relocations (e.g., X→V, V→X) and test them before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: Diagonal sticks are treated like any other stick, so the model may remove one without checking that the source character remains a valid numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After removing a diagonal, verify that the originating character still matches a known Roman numeral; if not, discard that move.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on symbolic validity and forgets that the numeric equality must also hold.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compute the integer values of both sides immediately after confirming symbol validity; reject any transformation that does not satisfy the arithmetic.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: Swapping operators seems to balance the equation superficially, but the equality sign may become invalid or disappear.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When altering an operator, explicitly check that the final equation still contains a valid '=' sign with two horizontal sticks.

matchstick.description: Forgetting to place the removed stick after modifying an operator (e.g., converting plus to minus) and leaving it unused
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often treats the removed stick as discarded rather than as a resource to be reused.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat the removed stick as a free piece that must be attached elsewhere (e.g., to augment a numeral) before finalizing the solution.
